result.summary: Shopify product-feed cleanup sprint for small merchants with live Google Shopping or Meta catalog traffic.
result.opportunity: Many small Shopify stores have messy product titles, variants, image references, GTIN/MPN fields, unit names or CSV exports. Google explicitly states that accurate, correctly formatted product data is foundational for ads and free listings, and missing or conflicting data can cause disapprovals, limited eligibility and poor display quality.
result.target_customer: Small DTC Shopify stores in Spain/Europe with 30-300 SKUs, active Google Shopping or Meta catalog traffic, and obvious product data inconsistencies in titles, variants, image mappings or CSV exports.
result.offer: A fixed-scope Shopify feed cleanup sprint: audit up to 100 SKUs, correct titles, variant names, URLs, image references, units, GTIN/MPN fields, duplicate rows and CSV export quality, then deliver a cleaned feed snapshot plus a 1-page QA checklist. Optional expansion to the next SKU batch after validation.
result.price: 149 EUR for up to 100 SKUs; 299 EUR for up to 300 SKUs or full catalog
result.why_now: Google Merchant Center documentation says product data quality is essential for successful ads and free listings, and missing or incorrect attributes can lead to disapprovals or limited eligibility. This is a direct, visible operational pain for merchants with live catalogs and offers a low-cost, bounded fix that can be sold without building a full SaaS.
actions_completed: Reviewed repository context and recent competitor attempts in the local market.
Reviewed the monetization playbook and the relevant seeds #18, #38 and adjacent productized service routes.
Inspected CobrAMO payment infrastructure and confirmed it is a payment receiver only, not a customer database.
Confirmed the current market pain from Google Merchant Center documentation on feed quality and product-data requirements.
Prepared a concrete execution packet for a fixed-scope Shopify feed cleanup offer with the required RANK-IAMO498 attribution.

execution_packet.channel: Email from the public storefront contact form or business email, sent to a single merchant owner with one clear observation and no mass outreach.
execution_packet.subject: Quick feed QA for [Store Name] — 3 catalog issues affecting Google Shopping
execution_packet.message: Hola [Nombre], vi que tu catálogo de Shopify tiene varios elementos que suelen dañar el rendimiento en Google Shopping y Meta: títulos poco consistentes, variantes con nombres desalineados, URLs o referencias de imagen duplicadas, o campos GTIN/MPN/units poco claros. Esto no suele ser un problema de marketing, sino de calidad del feed. He preparado un sprint fijo de limpieza de feed para revisar hasta 100 SKUs y dejar un CSV/snapshot corregido con una checklist de QA. La entrega incluye: limpieza de títulos y variantes, revisión de imágenes/URLs, corrección de unidades y campos de producto, y un chequeo de duplicados y exportación. Si te interesa, puedo hacer un mini-audit de 3 productos como ejemplo sin compromiso. Mi referencia comercial es RANK-IAMO498. Si te parece útil, te envío una muestra en 24h y te propongo el paquete por 149 EUR. Gracias por tu tiempo.
execution_packet.deliverable: Cleaned product-feed snapshot in CSV/Excel, corrected SKU list, 1-page QA checklist, before/after sample and remediation notes for the next batch.

result.differentiation_from_previous: I did not repeat the crowded local-review or GBP-only pattern. This is a more operational, easier-to-prove offer tied directly to merchant catalogs: quality product feed issues are explicit in Google Merchant Center docs, and the fix is bounded, visible and low-friction to sell. It combines route #18 with the productized data-cleanup logic of route #38, but narrows the scope to one common merchant outcome: stronger Google Shopping feed quality and fewer catalog errors.
result.next_step: Identify 15-20 active Shopify stores in Spain/Europe with public product catalogs and visible title/variant inconsistencies; send one short personalized message with 2-3 concrete issues; if they respond, send a 3-product sample audit and close the first 149 EUR cleanup through CobrAMO using reference RANK-IAMO498.
result.notes: This is a low-cost, fixed-scope validation path, not a revenue claim. The market evidence is from official Google Merchant Center guidance. Relevant playbook routes considered: #18 Shopify app or merchant helper, #38 Data migration or cleanup package, and nearby productized-service patterns for SEO/data cleanup; the chosen angle stays narrower and more measurable than generic GBP or dashboard offers.
